Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — sizing input for next sprint

Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We had a quick internal follow-up: the engineering team needs a tight estimate on the Dedicated pool we should reserve for our initial production rollout in September. High-level ask below — can your infra folks confirm feasibility and a rough GPU count?

- Expected peak concurrent sessions: 120 (90 external users + 30 internal batch jobs)
- Average request length: 800 tokens, bursts up to 3k tokens (30s windows)
- Target p99 latency: <350ms (for small interactive workflows)
- We expect steady growth: +25% month-over-month for first 3 months

I'm attaching our current MRR forecast and a basic usage curve. Procurement also needs an outline of commitment tiers so finance can evaluate.

Attachments: acme_mrr_forecast.xlsx

Can we get a quick alignment this week?

Thanks,
Jane

Hi Jane — looping in infra (Ben) and finance (Laura) to size this out. Quick read: we can get a workable committed pool + burst plan. Two early clarifying questions before Ben drafts numbers:

1) Are the 120 concurrent sessions sustained across a rolling hour or concentrated in a 10–20 minute peak window?
2) Do you plan to run heavy batch jobs during peak interactive traffic or scheduled off-peak?

Action: Ben to propose GPU count and basic reserve/commit tiers. Laura to flag any finance constraints for a monthly vs annual commit. I'll consolidate and share an action plan with ACME.

Best,

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — sizing input for next sprint

Thanks Tessa. Quick engineering take (back-of-envelope) based on the inputs and typical model footprints we run for ACME-style workloads:

Assumptions:
- Serving model: mix of 13B quantized and 70B q4f64 variants (interactive uses 13B; batch uses 70B)
- Avg tokens/sec per session: 25 (interactive)
- Effective concurrency headroom for batching: ~1.8x when inside burst windows

Proposal (initial):
- Committed pool: 12 GPUs (A100-style equivalent) sized to cover sustained interactive workload (target p95 latency under normal load)
- Burst reservation (on top): 6 GPUs on auto-burst / spot-like tier for short peaks (30–45m windows)
- Batch lane: 4 separate GPUs allocated to nightly/async jobs (can be scheduled outside peak)

Rationale: 12 committed + 6 burst + 4 batch = 22 GPUs total footprint. This gives ~18–24k concurrent tokens/sec capacity, with room for +25% growth for first two months.

Open questions for sizing accuracy:
- If ACME expects sustained peaks >20 minutes, we should increase committed pool.
- Quantization/placement changes can shift numbers — we can run a quick sim if they share a 24-hour request sample.

I'll attach a draft pool map (PDF) and a simple per-token cost delta estimate.

Attachments: proposed_pool_map.pdf

—Ben
Ben Carter | Infrastructure Planner, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Thanks all — finance notes below. High level: procurement wants 3 pricing tiers to evaluate (monthly commit, 6-month, annual). Key constraints: ACME's procurement policy has a preferred annual commit discount threshold at $X/month (redacted).

What we need to give them this week:
- Rough monthly cost for the committed pool (12 GPUs) + burst (6) + batch (4) under current per-GPU unit pricing
- An optional annual commitment projection with a simple discount ladder (5%/10%/15% at commit bands)
- Clause language for burst credits and overage accounting (we can propose pre-purchased burst credits redeemable for short windows)

Tessa — can you confirm whether ACME is open to a minimum 6-month commitment? If not, the monthly + burst credits model is likely the only path.

I'll prepare a one-pager cost summary and include a sample contract redline for procurement to review.

Laura Bennett | Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
